Draw: A plain band of brushed pewter: a cool mid-gray metal with a fine vertical grain, a slightly darker rolled lip along its left side and a thin bright highlight just inside it, otherwise quiet and even from top to bottom. Understated — it marks the card as altered without saying how.

A band of burnished gold leaf: warm deep yellow metal with a raised, slightly rounded profile, a dark amber rolled lip along its left side, a bright near-white highlight running down the crest, and small irregular flecks and cracks where the leaf has been laid by hand. It should read unmistakably as real gold even when only a sliver of the left side shows.

A band of polished sterling silver: cool, bright, white metal with a near-mirror finish, a dark blue-gray tarnished lip along its left side, a crisp near-white highlight running down the crest, and faint fine scratches and small hammered dimples along its length. It should read unmistakably as silver rather than steel or pewter — brighter, whiter and more reflective — even when only a sliver of the left side shows.

A band of wet watercolor running through five colors from top to bottom — orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, in that order, each roughly a fifth of the length — where each color bleeds into the next in soft, wavy, uneven tide-lines rather than straight joins, with pigment pooling darker at the wavy edges and granulating slightly. Luminous and saturated, as though painted over a thin gilded base that glints through the paler patches.

A band of three materials running from top to bottom — ivory, then steel, then granite, each roughly a third of the length — where each gives way to the next in soft, wavy, uneven seams rather than straight joins, as though the band were cast from all three at once. The ivory is smooth warm cream bone, the steel is brushed cool gray metal, the granite is speckled dark gray stone. A darker rolled lip runs down its left side through all three.

A band of rose quartz: translucent soft rose stone, polished smooth and faintly lit from within, with milky cloudy veins drifting slowly down its length and a darker deep-rose lip along its left side. Gentle and warm; it should read as a living, mending stone rather than as metal.

A band of hammered bronze: warm dark brown-gold metal, thick and heavy, its surface covered in overlapping round hammer marks like the face of a shield, with a raised rim along its left side studded with a row of small domed rivets running top to bottom, and a dull, battle-worn sheen.

A band of raw red copper: hot red-gold metal with a rough, freshly struck surface, a scorched near-black lip along its left side, and glowing ember-red cracks and nicks running down its length, as if it has just been pulled from the forge.

A band of deep garnet enamel set in dark gold: glossy wine-red vitreous enamel filling a channel, divided at irregular intervals down its length by thin gold cloisonné wires that branch and link into one another like the links of a chain, with a dark gold lip along its left side.

A band of verdigris-crusted bronze: a dull blue-green patina over dark metal, matte and still, with the bare dark bronze showing through only along a worn lip on its left side. It should feel dormant — strength being held back rather than spent.

A band of carved jade: dense, matte, pale sea-green stone with darker mottled clouds, carved with a shallow repeating ridge pattern that runs down its length like overlapping scales, and a darker lip along its left side. Quiet and heavy; it should feel like something kept rather than used.

A band of dark blued steel: deep slate-blue heat-tempered metal with a faint oily iridescence, quiet and cold, set with one line of tiny crimson garnet beads running down its length just inside a darker lip along its left side, like drops of blood held in reserve.
